Rates are currently cross-read, not sourced -- the vendor pricing page 403s -- and gpt-5-nano is DEFAULT_COMPARATOR_ID (cloudRates.ts:133), so every headline figure derives from an unsourced number. Usage-journal producer gate: after a full compile on a real box, assert the journal carries a record from EVERY producer the contract declares -- not >=1 of each kind. A >=1 predicate is a golden case and cannot give a denominator: nine producers with one writing passes forever. Absence with no compile having run must exit 2 CANNOT-RUN, not 1 FAIL. Gate must be wired to a path that executes and PROVED to fire -- ref #713/#719, where every box-walk probe returned SKIP for its whole life and nothing invoked the runner.

Engine provenance and disclosure: record what WE installed vs what was already on the box, derived from a before/after diff and never asserted. owner: customer|ostler|none|unknown. # 2026-08-25 -- v1.0.45's SEVEN ROWS CARRIED FORWARD AS REGRESSION GUARDS,
# THIS TIME WITH PREDICATES. Board #631, the open half.
# Six of v1.0.45's seven rows shipped with capability_id=none and verify=TBD.
# That combination asserts a fix is in the artefact while leaving nothing that
# could ever prove it, so the fix can regress in any later cut with every gate
# still green. verify_must_contain.sh counts those rows; it cannot refuse on
# them. These eight rows replace that with commands.
# #873 IS SPLIT IN TWO. Its v1.0.45 row carried two unrelated defects -- an
# ERR trap that recorded no failed step, and prose executing out of an unquoted
# heredoc. Different mechanisms, independently regressable, so two rows.
# HOW TO RUN THE verify COLUMN. Every command below reads the ARTEFACT.
#   M=/tmp/ostler-cut-mount && mkdir -p "$M"
#   hdiutil attach -readonly -nobrowse -mountpoint "$M" OstlerInstaller-<ver>.dmg

#   W="$M/OstlerInstaller.app/Contents/Resources/Ostler.app/Contents/MacOS/ostler-hub"
#   ... run the rows ... then: hdiutil detach "$M"
# hdiutil does NOT accept `--`; do not add one. install.sh and the strings
# catalogue ship as PLAIN TEXT inside OstlerInstaller.app, so they are directly
# greppable -- unlike the Hub SPA, which is embedded COMPRESSED and where a
# byte grep returns 0 for the subject AND for its control.
# 🔴 WHAT `landed=yes` MEANS HERE, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT.

# c4c5b40b, CM044 6b0492d -- and against the built v1.0.45 Hub, whose wrapper
# stamps WRAPPER_FRONTEND_COMMIT=c4c5b40b408e4f92ad85c89b882bafc756c0e3e3.

# takes this cut RE-RUNS the verify column against v1.0.46's own artefact
# before reading any row here as true. A row that has sat across two cuts has
# already been wrong once about which cut it was in.
# EVERY PREDICATE BELOW WAS WATCHED GOING RED. Two independent arms.
#   arm A  the SHIPPED v1.0.37 DMG, sha256 e6abc6b2d462d5d180c979ca6389def727

#          predicates report absent against it; its wrapper stamps
#          5b7efb00a54131bf49cb659ea3e23fb325e83db7 and still carries the nav

#   arm B  narrow single-marker mutations of the v1.0.45 pinned install.sh.
#          Six mutations, one identifier each: each killed EXACTLY ONE row and
#          left the other five IN. No row here is satisfied by a sibling.
# CANNOT-RUN IS NOT A PASS. If the DMG will not mount, or $I is absent, or a
# grep exits >=2, the row has not been verified -- say so and refuse. A zero

🟠 #873(a) A RUN THAT ABORTED AT A STEP REPORTED ZERO FAILED STEPS. From the v1.0.43 walk on the Mini, 2026-08-24T04:40:06Z: '[gui-marker] DONE status=fail code=ERR-99-INSTALL-ABORT-L2151 failed_steps=0' -- the install died INSIDE step fda_extract and the failed-step counter recorded nothing, so any consumer reading failed_steps rather than status saw a clean run. FIXED: _ostler_on_err is handed the real exit code by the ERR trap and calls gui_step_record_rc with it BEFORE gui_done closes the still-open step, so the STEP_END carries the code the command actually returned rather than the rc=1 convention.

column1: 🟠 #873(b) PROSE EXECUTED OUT OF AN UNQUOTED HEREDOC, ON THE CUSTOMER'S BOX. 'install.sh: line 9979: convert: command not found' in Andy's v1.0.43 transcript was NOT a missing ImageMagick dependency -- that diagnosis is wrong and the v1.0.45 row carried it. The .env heredoc is unquoted BY NECESSITY (it interpolates USER_ID and two dozen more), and an unquoted heredoc runs command substitution on its body as well as expanding parameters. A COMMENT reading `convert --source apple_notes` inside it RAN, bash reported the failure at the enclosing cat, and the substitution's empty output was written into the customer's .env. DO NOT 'fix' this by installing ImageMagick. FIXED by escaping every backtick and $( in the body.
column6: awk '/<<ENVEOF$/{h=1;next} h&&/^ENVEOF$/{h=0} h' "$I" | /usr/bin/grep -cE '(^|[^\\])(`|\$\()'  # expect 0 live substitutions. CONTROL: the same awk must emit 46 lines on both arms, so a 0 means clean and not empty. RED-PROVED: 1 on the shipped v1.0.37 DMG, and it is the real defect -- the live `convert` prose line. DEEPER RE-PROOF, and it carries its own denominator: copy $I and install.sh.strings.en-GB.sh out of the DMG into a dir, put CM051 tests/ beside them, run tests/test_no_live_command_substitution_in_heredocs.sh -- rc=0 on v1.0.45, rc=1 on v1.0.37, 53 heredocs scanned of which 25 unquoted.

column1: 🟠 #875 THE INSTALLER RE-ASKED THE iPHONE/TAILSCALE SETUP ON AN UPGRADE, a question the disk already answers. Andy mid-walk: 'that should've already been done last install time, no?' -- and ~/.ostler/tailscale/tailscaled.state was 2,863 bytes dated 2026-08-21, with tailscaled already running. The old detection branch tested whether the BINARY was installed, not whether tailnet STATE existed: the weaker of the two questions was the only one asked. An upgrade that re-interrogates the user about settled state reads as a reinstall. FIXED: _ts_already_configured parses the state store and is THREE-STATE -- 0 configured, 1 not configured, 2 CANNOT-RUN -- and existence and size are both explicitly rejected as discriminators, because tailscaled writes the store before any login so the file exists, well-formed and non-empty, on a box that never signed in. An unreadable store WARNS AND ASKS rather than reading as configured, and a human 'skip' this run outranks anything on disk.
column6: /usr/bin/grep -cE '^elif _ts_already_configured; then' "$I"  # expect 2 -- BOTH prompt sites, guarded at the PROMPT rather than merely defining the helper. CONTROL and denominator: /usr/bin/grep -cE 'gui_read "\$MSG_PROMPT_TAILSCALE_CONFIRM_TITLE"' "$I" is 2 on BOTH arms, so the denominator is 2 of 2 guarded at v1.0.45 and 0 of 2 at v1.0.37 -- a skip proved only by the present-state arm would not be proved. RED-PROVED: 0 on the shipped v1.0.37 DMG. DEEPER: tests/test_tailscale_prompt_is_conditional_on_tailnet_state.sh, staged the same way: 40 passed / 0 failed on v1.0.45, 14 passed / 14 failed on v1.0.37 -- and the three v1.0.37 failures that matter are EMPTY / CORRUPT / UNREADABLE state files, which asked without warning, i.e. CANNOT-RUN had no appearance of its own.

column1: 🔴🔴 #876 THE INSTALLER TOLD THE CUSTOMER THE DOCTOR WAS RUNNING AND IT WAS NOT. On the v1.0.44 walk install.sh printed 'Ostler Doctor running at http://localhost:8089/doctor' while com.ostler.doctor was NOT LOADED and :8089 answered 000. Six customer surfaces were dark behind that one line and the log recorded a clean run. Two independent reasons the old shape could not be trusted: `bootstrap … || load … || true` terminates the chain so no path does NOT print success; and `launchctl load` on a missing plist prints 'Load failed: 5' to stderr and EXITS 0, so even the if/else form was unconditionally true and its else had never once run. FIXED by one helper that boots out, bootstraps, falls back to load, and THEN asks launchd -- and reads the OUTPUT of launchctl print, not its exit code, because print returns 0 for a merely REGISTERED job; it refuses on 'last exit code = 78' (EX_CONFIG, which launchd does not retry) specifically rather than on any non-zero, since several agents are periodic and legitimately exit non-zero.
column6: /usr/bin/grep -cE '^[[:space:]]*(if|elif) _ostler_launchagent_load_verified "' "$I"  # expect 11 CALL SITES. 🔴 USE THIS ROW, NOT doctor_load_is_verified: MEASURED on a mutant with all eleven sites routed around the helper, doctor_load_is_verified (hits 15->4) and doctor_ok_not_unconditional (0->0) BOTH still read IN. Presence of a helper is not use of it. CONTROL: /usr/bin/grep -cE 'launchctl bootstrap "gui/' "$I" is non-zero on both arms (8 at v1.0.45, 17 at v1.0.37). RED-PROVED: 0 on the shipped v1.0.37 DMG and 0 on the route-around mutant. DEEPER, and it is the only thing here that gives the true denominator: tests/test_launchagent_success_requires_verification.sh staged against the artefact -- v1.0.45 PASS 6/FAIL 0 with '33 bootstrap/load sites scanned, 0 announcements not backed by launchd, floor 11'; v1.0.37 PASS 0/FAIL 14.

column1: # 2026-08-25 -- FOUND BY WALKING v1.0.45 ON HARDWARE, NOT BY A GATE.
# The v1.0.45 DMG passed 14 of 14 artefact checks -- bytes, sha256 vs
# SHA256SUMS, spctl, stapler, inner .app version, install.sh read out of the
# mount with a line-count control. Every one of those checks read the app on
# a READ-ONLY volume. The defect below only exists once the app is copied
# somewhere WRITABLE, which is the only place a customer ever runs it.
# THE LESSON, AND IT IS THE SAME ONE AS THE COMPRESSED-SPA TRAP: a control
# that cannot exhibit the defect is not a control. Verifying the artefact at
# rest proved the bytes were right and said nothing about what the artefact
# DOES to itself when run. Every future installer check that can be run
# against a writable copy should be.

🔴🔴 THE INSTALLER BREAKS ITS OWN CODE SIGNATURE ON FIRST RUN AND MACOS THEN REFUSES IT AS "damaged and can't be opened. You should move it to the Bin." -- MEASURED ON HARDWARE 2026-08-25 during Andy's v1.0.45 walk, on a DMG that had already been independently artefact-verified (58,099,134 bytes, sha256 70ebd92631688d8291dac4b113ac3f7397711fb37f81fdfc48dee23971989b57, spctl Notarized Developer ID, stapled). MECHANISM: the app ships ZERO .pyc (measured: find -name '*.pyc' = 0 on the mounted DMG), so the FIRST time the bundled interpreter at Contents/Resources/python/bin/python3.11 runs from a WRITABLE location it compiles its own stdlib and writes Contents/Resources/python/lib/python3.11/__pycache__/{secrets,hmac,platform}.cpython-311.pyc INSIDE the signed bundle. Any file ADDED to a signed bundle voids the seal: codesign --verify --deep --strict said 'a sealed resource is missing or invalid' and named exactly 3 added files, 3 of 3 __pycache__. 🔴 AND THE VERDICT STICKS AFTER THE DAMAGE IS UNDONE. Deleting the 3 .pyc restored the seal (codesign 'valid on disk', spctl 'accepted / Notarized Developer ID') and the dialog STILL respawned on every launch, because Gatekeeper had cached the damaged assessment against the com.apple.quarantine record Safari attached. It took TWO removals to unblock a human who was mid-walk: rm the __pycache__ AND xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine. A customer has neither. THIS REACHES EVERY CUSTOMER: quarantine is attached by every browser download, and the failure is on FIRST RUN, not on relaunch. FIX: the bundled interpreter must never write into the bundle. Set PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX to a writable dir outside Contents/ (keeps the caching) or PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 (drops it), at EVERY site that invokes it -- not one. MEASURED: install.sh sets neither today (grep -c 'PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE\|PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX' = 0). Pre-compiling at build time so the .pyc sit INSIDE the signature is the other valid shape; either way the gate below is what proves it, because both fixes are invisible to a source grep if a single call site is missed. 🔴 WHAT THE HUMAN ACTUALLY SEES, AND IT IS NOT ONE DIALOG: syspolicyd refuses the EMBEDDED INTERPRETER, not the app. kernel AppleSystemPolicy logged 'ASP: Security policy would not allow process: <pid>, /Applications/OstlerInstaller.app/Contents/Resources/python/bin/python3.11' with a FRESH PID roughly once a second (41247 41250 41251 41252 41253 41254 41255 41256 41257 41258 41259 41301 41302 41303 41304), each paired with syspolicyd 'Prompt shown (1,0), waiting for response' and 'Adding Gatekeeper denial breadcrumb (open)' -- the installer RETRIES, so cancelling the dialog just summons the next one and the customer cannot progress or escape. The app itself launches and dies (loginwindow logs appDeath for ai.ostler.installer). GK evaluateScanResult: 3. RECOVERY NEEDED THREE REMOVALS, and any one alone left it broken: (1) rm the __pycache__ that voided the seal, (2) xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine, (3) the com.apple.provenance record, which macOS 26 keeps SEPARATELY from quarantine and which stripping quarantine does NOT clear. Verified afterwards: 0 files carrying quarantine, 0 carrying provenance, 0 .pyc, codesign 'valid on disk', and the interpreter then ran real installer work (python3.11 -m compiler.emit_artefact). ⚠️ I GOT THIS WRONG TWICE BEFORE READING THE LOG -- first 'bad download' (refuted: sha256 matched the published release exactly), then 'stale cached Gatekeeper verdict' (incomplete: it was live refusals of a different binary). The system log named the subject in one line. Read it before theorising.
column6: ARTEFACT-LEVEL, and it must be run against a WRITABLE COPY -- the defect cannot appear on the read-only DMG, which is exactly why every prior artefact check passed. M=/tmp/ostler-cut-mount && mkdir -p "$M" && hdiutil attach -readonly -nobrowse -mountpoint "$M" <dmg>  (hdiutil does NOT accept --); T="$(mktemp -d)" && ditto "$M/OstlerInstaller.app" "$T/OstlerInstaller.app"; "$T/OstlerInstaller.app/Contents/Resources/python/bin/python3.11" -c 'import secrets,hmac,platform'; codesign --verify --deep --strict --verbose=2 "$T/OstlerInstaller.app" 2>&1 | /usr/bin/grep -c '^file added:'  # EXPECT 0. DENOMINATOR, same copy, and it is the number that makes the 0 mean something: find "$T/OstlerInstaller.app" -name '*.pyc' | wc -l  # EXPECT 0; on v1.0.45 it is 3 AFTER the import and 0 BEFORE, so a 0 recorded without running the interpreter proves nothing. CONTROL that must stay GREEN or the test is measuring the wrong thing: spctl -a -t exec -vv "$M/OstlerInstaller.app" is 'accepted / Notarized Developer ID' on v1.0.45 -- the DMG copy was never the problem. RED-PROVED ON REAL HARDWARE, not a fixture: /Applications/OstlerInstaller.app on the Mac mini, 2026-08-25 15:45 local, 3 file-added lines / 3 __pycache__ / spctl 'a sealed resource is missing or invalid'. 🔴 CANNOT-RUN IS NOT A PASS: if the DMG will not mount, if that python3.11 path is absent, if ditto fails, or if codesign exits >=2, the row has NOT been verified -- say so and refuse. A grep count of 0 from a command that could not look is indistinguishable on screen from a 0 that means the defect is gone.

column1: 🔴 DONE status=ok WITH failed_steps=3 -- THE MIRROR OF #873, AND #873's FIX DID NOT COVER IT. Measured on the Mac mini's ~/.ostler/logs/install.log, final two lines of the v1.0.44 run: 'STEP_END id=health_check status=error elapsed_s=11 rc=2' immediately followed by '[gui-marker] DONE status=ok failed_steps=3'. #873 was the case where an ABORT reported failed_steps=0; this is the case where a run that COMPLETED with three failed steps reports status=ok. Same broken relationship between the summary verdict and the counter, opposite direction, and the v1.0.45 fix (installer_abort_records_failed_step) guards only the abort limb -- it makes the COUNTER right and says nothing about the VERDICT. Any consumer reading status rather than failed_steps sees a clean install. REQUIRED: DONE status must be DERIVED from failed_steps, not written independently, so the two cannot disagree in either direction; and health_check rc=2 is CANNOT-RUN, which must not silently become a failed step nor a pass.
column5: TBD -- add capability row done_status_derives_from_failed_steps WITH the fix
column6: ARTEFACT + RUN LEVEL, and it needs a real install log, so it is a box-walk row not a static grep. On the run's install.log: n=$(/usr/bin/grep -c 'STEP_END .*status=error' "$LOG"); then /usr/bin/grep -E '^\[gui-marker\] DONE ' "$LOG" | tail -1 -- assert failed_steps == $n AND (n>0 implies status!=ok). CONTROL, so a 0 cannot be a failed look: /usr/bin/grep -c 'STEP_END' "$LOG" must be >0 (38 on the v1.0.44 run). column1: 🟠 I EXECUTED CODE INTO MY OWN BOM ROW, WHICH IS THE #873(b) DEFECT COMMITTED BY ITS OWN AUTHOR. Writing the row above via bin/bom_add.sh, I put a backticked command inside the `what` argument in a double-quoted shell context. The shell ran it. bom_add.sh printed the command's OUTPUT ('Bad request. Could not find service...') and wrote a row with the command MISSING from it -- a register entry silently short of the evidence it claimed to carry. Same mechanism as the .env heredoc that put 'convert: command not found' in a customer transcript, same afternoon, by the person who filed it. NOT A COSMETIC POINT: this register is the thing a cut is gated on, and any row written through a double-quoted shell argument can lose content this way without anyone noticing -- the tool exits 0 and the row looks plausible. REQUIRED: bom_add.sh must refuse, or neutralise, live command substitution in its arguments -- reject an unescaped ` or $( in `what` with a non-zero exit and a message naming the offending character, rather than writing a quietly truncated row.

The DAEMON serves on 8000 (curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/health -> 200). The CLI loads the ROOT one -- it prints 'Config loaded path=/Users/andy/.ostler/config.toml' -- so 'ostler-assistant gateway get-paircode' tries 127.0.0.1:42617, fails to connect, and tells the operator 'Is the gateway running? Either the removal targets a different path than the writer, or something recreates it afterwards. IMPACT BEYOND PAIRING: this is the config every CLI subcommand resolves, so it breaks the whole recovery surface at exactly the moment a customer needs it -- when the GUI is already stuck. Found while recovering Andy from a 401 reconnect loop; the only route that worked was hitting /admin/paircode on 8000 directly with the admin token.

🔴🔴 LAUNCH BLOCKER, RE-DIAGNOSED -- AND MY FIRST DIAGNOSIS ON THIS ROW WAS WRONG, SO READ THIS ONE. WITHDRAWN: 'the app pairs on 8443, which rejects every code the gateway issues'. That is REFUTED. The pairing code is SINGLE-USE BY DESIGN -- zeroclaw-config/src/pairing.rs:168 sets *pairing_code = None inside try_pair_blocking the instant a code matches. So posting ONE code to two ports can never succeed twice, whichever port goes first, and my experiment was incapable of producing any other result. My control (a wrong code is refused on 8443) proved the PREDICATE and said nothing about the SPECIMEN. THE DAEMON LOG SETTLES IT, ostler-assistant.err lines 128-132, one mint and three posts inside 123ms: 08:47:17.921 'New pairing envelope generated via admin endpoint' -> 08:47:17.995 'New client paired successfully' -> 08:47:18.037 'Pairing attempt with invalid code' -> 08:47:18.044 same. The FIRST post won and spent the code; the other two lost a race, 42ms and 49ms later. Not a port defect. 🔴 WHAT IS ACTUALLY BROKEN, AND IT IS STILL A LAUNCH BLOCKER: THE HUB APP RE-PAIRS IN A LOOP AND SHOWS THE CUSTOMER THE LOSER'S 403. MEASURED, same log, 08:41:00 to 08:46:04: ~25 'New client paired successfully' in five minutes, in BURSTS OF FIVE with gaps of 2.2s / 3.0s / 4.4s / 7.5s / 13.4s, then a pause over 60s, then another burst of five. That is the exact signature of web/src/hooks/useAuth.ts RECOVER_MAX_ATTEMPTS=5, RECOVER_BASE_DELAY_MS=750 doubling, RECOVER_RESET_MS=60000. PERSISTED PROOF ON DISK, and it is the number that makes this undeniable: ~/.ostler/assistant-config/config.toml carries 34 paired_tokens (34 'enc2:' entries, 6578 bytes on ONE line) -- one leaked token per re-pair, never revoked, growing without bound. ROOT CAUSE IS NOT THE LOOP -- THE LOOP IS THE DESIGNED SYMPTOM HANDLER. useAuth.ts:146-154 says in terms that doPair deliberately does NOT reset the recovery budget, so the machinery is behaving to spec. The fault is UPSTREAM: something 401s immediately after each SUCCESSFUL pair, and Andy's own screenshots name the surfaces -- both the People and the Timeline panes render the literal string UNAUTHORIZED while the app claims to be connected. Find what 401s with a token the gateway minted one second earlier; the re-pair storm and the 'Pairing failed (403)' Andy photographed are both downstream of it. CUSTOMER IMPACT UNCHANGED FROM THE WITHDRAWN VERSION, so do not downgrade the priority: an upgrade restarts the daemon, the restart kills the session, and the app's only offered recovery is a pairing flow that machine-guns itself and surfaces a 403. ⚠️ DO NOT RE-RUN MY ORIGINAL EXPERIMENT. Any test that posts one code to two ports and calls the second rejection a failure will fail on a HEALTHY system. Assert the property (a freshly minted code pairs exactly once, and a session that dies can be re-established without the customer typing anything), never the two-port comparison.
